text:
Maria: Heads-up — nf4 canary on eu-dedicated shows a ~18% throughput drop at p95 for chat workloads after the quant kernel swap. NVLINK counters spike and we see repeated cudaMemcpy stalls. Repro on canary nodes. :eyes:

Ajay: Link to the raw canary report?

Maria: s3://redwood-perf/canaries/2051234567/nf4-canary-report.html

Lee: What were the batch/seq shapes? any prefix caching or special batching flags?

Maria: batch=4/8, seq=1024, prefix caching ON, batching=auto. Repro command I used:

```bash
python -m perf.run --model redwood/nf4-v2.2 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --quant nf4 --prefetch --batching=auto
```

Devon: Sounds like allocator fragmentation + extra host<->device copies. We saw something similar after the TCMalloc bump — small alloc churn killed coalescing. Any allocator flag diffs?

Maria: No allocator flag changes on canary. The new quant kernel includes a fused CPU->quant prep step and per-thread workspace allocations. Profiling shows long stalls at cuLaunchKernel for "quant_matmul_n4" and spikes of memcpy H2D right before. KV hit rate unchanged.

perf-bot: perf: uploaded flamegraphs and nvprof timeline to s3://redwood-perf/traces/2051234567/ (flame.html, nvprof.nv)

Ajay: If it's per-op workspace growth, try running with split-k or lowering batch to see linearity. Also toggle the runtime flag that moves quant prep to device if available.

Lee: Could be alignment/stride issues in the fused kernel causing driver to fall back to slower memcpy paths. Bisect the kernel commit that introduced the fused path?

Maria: Local quick test: setting runtime.use_cpu_quant_prep=false bumped throughput ~7% (still ~11% below old baseline). Next test: kernels.disable_fused_preconversion=true to isolate fused code.

Devon: Also run jemalloc/tcmalloc per-thread slab stats; if batching heuristic now creates many tiny tensors we get fragmentation. Synthetic tests with mixed batch shapes helped us before.

Ajay: Add a matrix of synthetic runs across seq=[64,128,256,512,1024] and batch=[1,2,4,8] and include calib ON/OFF. If calibration changes the kernel selection it might explain different code paths.

Maria: On it. I’ll start the synthetic sweep tonight and upload CSV. Will run both pinned-calib=false and pinned-calib=true (auto-calib was rolled on in canary).

Lee: Note: calibration can flip to a fallback FP16 path for certain activation ranges — check kernel selection logs (runtime.debug.kernels=1).

Maria: Good call. I’ll collect kernel selection traces and per-op workspace sizes. Also will try forcing the older quant table (pre-rollout) to see if that recovers perf.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary health alert: regression >10% detected for 20m. Automatic rollback scheduled in 40m unless mitigations posted.

Devon: If rollback needed, coordinate with infra for a targeted revert so we can continue bisecting on a non-production fleet.

Maria: Will update with traces + slab stats in ~3h. Devon/Lee/Ajay — ping me if you want live access to a canary node. :thumbsup:

Ajay: Thanks — once we have traces we can narrow whether it's host-side conversion or kernel memory semantics. If host-side, quick revert of CPU->quant prep might recover most of perf.

Maria: Uploading now. Will post final synthetic CSV and nvprof tar in thread when done.
